To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the U5MR is declining, 2) the rate of decline is accelerating, 3) most of the decline is due to a reduction in the neonatal mortality rate, and 4) the decline is not uniform across regions or countries [5] The MDG 4 target is to reduce the 1990 U5MR by two thirds.

The U5MR in 2011 in the 75 low and middle income countries (LMICs) that have reported to the UN was 76/1,000 live births, a decline of 2.7% from the 78/1,000 reported in 1990 [5] The 2011 U5MR in the 15 LMICs with the highest burden of child deaths, accounting for 65% of the global total, was 117/1

progress in pediatric pharmacotherapy has been slow, but steady, with some significant achievements in the past few years.
the MDG 4 goal of a two thirds reduction in U5MR by 2015 will be difficult to achieve.

we are still far from achieving the Millennium Goals.
we are still a long way from having the right drugs for the right child at the right dose at the right time.
we are not doing enough, and not doing it fast enough.

the Millennium Campaign is a powerful force for change.
